## 1. The gen-3 batch witnesses are withdrawn; the batch face re-anchors (re-anchor change set `8e360cd`)

The gen-3 batch-bridge witnesses (`m7_floor_calibration_p7cap_20261104T093543Z`,
image r1, digest `dd8bc22a…`) were minted 2026-11-04 — four days before P10
landed and six before P11 — so their exported kernel predates both perf
phases and every ratio the census quoted for the batch arm carried
stale-kernel drag (commit `0cc9086`, PR #105). They are withdrawn per the
9a34548 pattern, quoted verbatim from the re-anchor change-set bytes:

> The gen-3 batch-bridge witnesses (m7_floor_calibration_p7cap_20261104T093543Z)
> predate the P11 kernel and pre-cap wall!=cpu bytes can never satisfy the
> post-cap witness law. They are withdrawn per the 9a34548 pattern: 21 witness
> files git-rm'd, their 21 rows stripped from CALIBRATION.json's witness_sha256
> (empty map, only-map-changed probe asserted); the ledger and anchors fragment
> stay as provenance.

The batch face re-anchors onto the sanctioned r2 re-mint
`m7_floor_calibration_p6_20261115-023000` (PR #105, squash-merge `0cc9086`,
merge 2026-11-15). Re-mint provenance, quoted from the commit-object bytes
and the campaign's `CALIBRATION.json`:

* Same witnessed tree `15b827981dd1a4be28207eb084f78140b70f8f09`, same
  ns/version/face bytes; exported msuiter kernel overlay resolved to
  `a0486b4` (post-P11 head; zero `src/rust` drift `a0486b4..origin/main`).
* Captured digest `sha256:b06cae931edab2805b94ad4b7d141257a308fff40c53a08e3901d04ce52b2d2f`
  by the SS3 inspect ceremony (`docker image inspect`, never transcribed);
  image ref `msuiter-sigminer:p6-sigminer_post_v3_rust_batch-r2`; tool
  version `2.3.3`. Revision 1 → 2 per the rust-twin precedent; runner/
  self-witness/Dockerfile recipe bytes untouched (byte-frozen arm recipe law).
* 21/21 cells rc=0 verdict OK at REP-100 (protocol scale), all attested
  live: `attestation=lv1(preflight='GO',coex='NOT-FLAT',epoch='b1ce0f176cec2633')`
  on all 21 census lines. `campaign_note` verbatim: "batch-bridge arm
  re-mint onto the post-P11 kernel r2 image (2026-11-15, campaign
  m7_floor_calibration_p6_20261115-023000); 21/21 cells rc=0 verdict OK,
  coex inversion-probe record bound to this campaign (T5)".
* Coex inversion probe (bound to this campaign): verdict **NOT-FLAT**,
  bar_pct 5.0, deltas_pct `[10.8, 10.8, 10.8]` (shape coex-inversion/N=3),
  solo_mean_s 408.761741, measured_utc `2026-11-14T18:57:16Z`; preflight GO
  recorded per witness (first: cell
  `sigminer_post_v3_rust_batch__clock__N1000`,
  ts `2026-11-14T21:08:02+00:00`).

The old image's 19 witness JSONs stay append-only under the 20261104
calibration dir — the withdrawal removes only the 21 census-facing gen-3
witnesses, never history.

## 2. The yardstick re-stamp and the epoch re-pin

The legacy yardstick (`m7_floor_calibration_p7cap_legacy_20261111-144552`)
witnesses are re-stamped onto `b1ce0f176cec2633` (attestation.epoch only;
an only-epoch-diff probe asserted every other field byte-stable;
`witness_sha256` maps recomputed after the stamp). The live epoch pins move
accordingly (`bench/m7/tests/test_p6_floor_governance.py`):

```
:173  PRECAP_SEALED_EPOCH = "6b3a66bc9d0224eb"      # measured before the flip
:174  POST_CAP_EPOCH_PIN = "b1ce0f176cec2633"   # measured; set at the 2026-11-15 batch-bridge r2 re-mint (r2 anchors registered; supersedes cfdcc51dbb9b7041)
```

The governance constants re-point in the same change set
(`bench/m7/tools/matrix_governance.py:1072-1075`): the r2 prefix
`POST_CAP_R2_REMINT_PREFIX = "m7_floor_calibration_p6_20261115-"` is
**date-scoped** so the pre-cap `p6_20261017` mint diverges at the date
digits; `POST_CAP_AUTHORITY_PREFIX = "m7_floor_calibration_p7cap_"` and
`POST_CAP_LEGACY_PREFIX = "m7_floor_calibration_p7cap_legacy_"` stand
unchanged. The 168 arithmetic is unchanged per line: 126
(p7cap_20261025-125823 gen-2 post-cap) + 21 (r2 re-mint) + 21 (legacy
083955 face) = 168 census lines = 8 faces × 21 classes.

Epoch doctrine: a re-stamp touches ONLY `attestation.epoch` — this is the
second such re-stamp in the chain (cfdcc51dbb9b7041 → b1ce0f176cec2633,
following the 2026-11-11 SS3 re-stamp f3e894a6933a2ffb → cfdcc51dbb9b7041),
both applications of the same post-cap witness law (the current pin must
name the epoch the post-cap witnesses were minted under), not new law. If
review judges it otherwise, the phase PR is where that ruling surfaces.

## 5. What this erratum deliberately does not claim

* No parity row: 168/168 BREACH is the census, and CAMPAIGN-R stays closed
  on the system-level <=2x row. The r2 re-anchor tightens the batch face's
  band (8.7963–17.7653 → 9.4409–14.2554 measured on the post-P11 kernel)
  and removes stale-kernel drag from every batch-arm ratio; it does not
  close any gate.
* No kernel-share figures: the 33.4% bridge-share estimate and the "2×
  measured-foreclosed for bit-identical code" characterization remain
  internal-ruling-only (memo `:166`, novelty-scan R1 row) — not committed
  measurements, not quoted as such here.
* No recipe edit: the r2 flip was a digest+revision data edit on PR #105;
  the byte-frozen arm recipe law held through this re-anchor (no
  runner/self-witness/Dockerfile byte changed).
* No census arithmetic change: the 126+21+21=168 accounting survives
  verbatim; only the 21-serving dir moves from the withdrawn gen-3 dir to
  the r2 dir, and every line's epoch moves with the pin.
